daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

President Prabowo has appointed 26 members to Wantimpres, including controversial commentator Rocky Gerung, Islamic scholar Quraish Shihab, and economist Sinta Nuriyah. The appointments signal Prabowo's effort to draw on diverse perspectives and considerations for his presidential advisory council. Rocky Gerung's inclusion has drawn particular attention given his past as a vocal critic of the previous administration.

  • National Police Chief Suyudi has ordered a major reshuffle affecting 88 high-ranking officers just two days after his inauguration, including the replacement of Metro Jaya Police Chief and the head of the Criminal Investigation Agency, with 19 regional police chiefs rotated nationwide.
  • The Constitutional Court is hearing challenges to Vice President Gibran's educational qualifications, with education attachés in Singapore and Australia testifying they found no documents related to Gibran's education at their embassies, though the Education Ministry stated his secondary education is equivalent to vocational high school.
  • A legal expert representing Gibran has filed a complaint with the Constitutional Court's ethics council after being ejected from a hearing.
  • Former Deputy Governor Gus Ipul has issued legal notices to three individuals over allegations of money flows during the NU Islamic organization's national congress.
  • A DPD member has submitted three recommendations to address problems with the accuracy of the national single education data system.
  • The Prosecutor General's Office (BGN) will take action against foundations demanding payments from partners in the Free Nutritious Meals (MBG) program, as the corruption investigation expands to include three additional suspects and alleged irregularities in electric motorcycle procurement.
  • The Home Affairs Minister and the Minister of Public Works and Housing jointly dispatched 125 trucks to support President Prabowo's roof-tile replacement program for low-income communities.

Foreign Policy & Defence

Indonesia's Deputy Foreign Minister urged continued cooperation to prevent tensions in the South China Sea, calling for a "habit of cooperation" among claimant states. The statement came as Indonesia reiterated its position on maintaining peace in contested waters. Separately, Russia emphasized the friendly nature of its naval visit to Indonesia.

  • Indonesia and Germany are looking to expand trade and investment cooperation, with Indonesia seeking to strengthen ties in industry and human resources development and pursue deeper strategic cooperation with Berlin.
  • Indonesia and the United States are strengthening marine research cooperation to address potential El Niño impacts in 2026-2027, while Indonesia is seeking U.S. oil technology to help reach its production target of one million barrels per day by 2030.
  • The leader of Russia's Republic of Tatarstan will visit Indonesia in early November, according to the Russian ambassador.
  • South Korea has opened employment opportunities for elderly care workers from Sumatra, with the ambassador noting that green and digital sectors are strengthening Indonesia-South Korea economic relations.
  • The Indonesian Migrant Worker Protection Agency (KP2MI) and Udayana University have established a Migrant Center to better prepare Indonesian migrant workers.

Other

The Financial Services Authority (OJK) has unveiled five priorities for Indonesia's banking sector through 2030, setting a strategic framework for the industry's development. Separately, the government is moving forward with plans for a state-owned insurance company merger, which is now being formulated by officials.

  • The government is preparing new income tax thresholds that would exempt workers earning up to the provincial minimum wage from taxation, according to leaked details of the proposed PTKP adjustments.
  • The Education Minister has urged universities to boost STEM graduates to meet industry needs and strengthen fundamental science programs.
  • The government has added 6,000 schools to its 2026 revitalization program, expanding infrastructure improvements nationwide.
  • Indonesia is accelerating aviation safety rules ahead of a 2027 ICAO audit, while an expert stated that the B50 biofuel program will allow Indonesia to stop diesel imports.
  • Police have dismantled a Malaysian drug network and seized 244 kilograms of methamphetamine, while separately seizing 57.88 kilograms of pangolin scales in South Kalimantan.
